exposure: body fluid type (mature breast milk, saliva, plasma)
outcome: N-glycosylation of SIgA/IgA (glycan compositions, proportions of high mannose, fucosylated, and sialylated glycans)
cohort: The participants were lactating mothers from whom breast milk, saliva, and plasma samples were collected.
finding: The study revealed a greater diversity of N-glycans than previously reported, with 89 glycan compositions (54 of which were body-fluid specific) across SIgA from mature milk and saliva, and plasma IgA.
mod_finding: Lactating participants who had given birth by vaginal delivery presented an increased proportion of high mannose and fucosylated glycans in salivary SIgA, and selected high mannose, fucosylated, sialylated, and both fucosylated and sialylated glycans in plasma IgA.
cross-section timing: During lactation, using mature breast milk samples
